drivers: A run of big overseas hacks and outages continues: China-linked hackers are suspected in the EU Commission and US intelligence breaches, and the US is probing whether Iran hacked up to 50 commercial ships. None has hit Australian banks, phones or power.

If the China-linked hacking is one deliberate campaign, the likely aim is quiet footholds in allies' phone, power and water networks ahead of any Taiwan crisis, with phone networks, utilities and ports the likely next targets; this is a hypothesis, though governments have blamed China for parts of it.
Suspected Iran-linked attacks on shop freezers, small water systems and ships remain overseas.

headline: Iran says another tanker hit a mine in Hormuz, but no new attacks on US bases were found and nothing has reached Australia.
summary: Iran's army says another oil tanker hit a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday; this is Iran's own claim, reported by its state media. No new confirmed attacks on US bases, and oil is steady at about US$90. The US is probing whether Iran hacked up to 50 commercial ships, and China-linked hacking of allies goes on, but Australian phones, banks and power are normal. Fire danger in the Hills is only Moderate today and tomorrow, with no CFS warnings near home.
